items.quote: The microstructures of all the alloy samples were observed using scanning electron microscope (SEM, Carl Zeiss LEO 1450) with energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS, Thermo Scientific UltraDry EDS).

items.applies_to: The alloys with the melting temperature below 1600 K
items.calibration: calibration material Al (TA Instruments-Waters LLC) as the standard sample
items.quote: The alloys with the melting temperature below 1600 K were examined using differential thermal analysis (DTA, TA Instruments SDT/ Q-600) with alumina crucibles under a flowing argon atmosphere. The heating and cooling rates were set as 10 K/min. Before testing, in order to eliminate the random errors and the systematic errors, the calibration of measurements was applied using the calibration material Al (TA Instruments-Waters LLC) as the standard sample.

After that, X-ray diffraction (XRD, Rigaku Ultima IV) with Cu-Kα radiation (voltage at 40 kV, current at 40 mA) in the 2θ range from 20 to 90° with a scan step 0.02° was applied to the powder samples.

items.label: Pr55B45
items.quote: The Pr-B binary alloys Pr55B45, Pr60B40, Pr65B35, Pr68B32 and Pr70B30, Pr-Fe binary alloys Pr58Fe42, Pr66Fe34 and Pr74Fe26 with the weight of 2 g and the Pr-Fe-B ternary alloys with the weight of 3 g were melted by a non-consumable tungsten electrode under a protective argon atmosphere at 0.105 MPa. Starting material of 99.99 wt% pure metal bulks of Pr, Fe and B (China New Metal Material Technology Company, Ltd.) were used. The alloys were melted for at least eight times to achieve melting homogenization.
items.starting_materials: metal bulks of Pr, Fe and B (China New Metal Material Technology Company, Ltd.)
